basis: Vulvar ulceration is confined to a reproductive organ outside the axes; no infectious or immune cause is specified.
A neurodevelopmental disorder defined by impaired communication and social development.
Structural brain malformations and severe developmental impairment define the syndrome; hypotonia is neurologic.
Collagen VI muscular dystrophy; progressive ventilatory failure affects >30% over the course. Isolated esodeviation reports do not establish common eye involvement.
Benign adipocytic tumor typically arising in subcutaneous tissue, which belongs to the dermatologic axis.
Inherited glutathione metabolic disorders; hemolysis and neurologic injury vary by subtype, with no established group-wide frequency supporting extra axes.
Carcinoma originating in the penis, a reproductive organ outside the axes; no other organ involvement is established.
Osteosarcoma occupying multiple bone sites; all defining sites belong to the musculoskeletal axis.
Thyroid enlargement caused by defective thyroid hormone synthesis; no additional common organ damage is established.
Degenerative cerebellar and pyramidal dysfunction; gaze palsy and ocular dysmetria reflect neurologic dysfunction rather than intrinsic eye disease.
Developmental, intestinal/salivary and hearing dysfunction define the syndrome; lacrimal failure occurs in 2/2. Recurrent airway mucus plugging omitted at the four-axis cap.
Congenital hip dysplasia and dislocation in 4/4 reported patients; confined to the skeletal system.
Nonsyndromic fusion of the tibia and fibula with associated limb and joint deformities.
Estrogen receptor resistance; osteoporosis and delayed skeletal maturation affect 80–99%. Coronary atherosclerosis is a separate disease; acanthosis is not organ dysfunction.
B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma is a hematopoietic malignancy; lymphoma also requires the infectious_immune mechanism axis.
Bone fragility, fractures and interosseous membrane mineralization define OI type V; dental disease is absent and scleral color does not imply eye damage.
Gonococcal infection of the seminal vesicles; infection supplies an axis although the reproductive site has none.
Developmental brain disorder; strabismus in 2/6 and craniosynostosis in 1/3 support eye and skeletal involvement, with uncertain estimates from small samples.
Skeletal dysplasia affecting vertebrae, epiphyses and metaphyses; no common independent extraskeletal damage is established.
Malignancy located in the nasal cavity, included in the upper respiratory tract; lymphoma and neural tumors are subtypes rather than group-wide mechanisms.
DM1 muscle disease; cognitive/developmental impairment affects most juvenile cases. Cardiac conduction disease and cataracts each affect >30% over the lifetime.
Neoplasm directly occupying the lumbar peripheral nerve plexus.
A neonatal platelet deficiency; an infectious or immune mechanism is not inherent to this umbrella concept.
Malignancy involving the pyriform sinus of the hypopharynx; the pharynx belongs to the pulmonary axis.
Congenital structural anomaly of the nose, explicitly included in the pulmonary axis; no other organ involvement is supplied.
